memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The total number of the men of Israel was 601,730. The LORD said to Moses, "The land is to be allotted to them as an inheritance based on the number of names. To a larger group give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group a smaller one; each is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those listed." - Num 26:51-54 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The census reaches its total: over six hundred thousand men. Then God gives instruction about the land. It would be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, each receiving a portion according to its size. The counting was not for its own sake; it was preparation for the gift of the Promised Land that lay ahead.

Here we see God as the giver of inheritance. The land was not something Israel earned or seized by their own power; it was a gift from the Lord, promised long before and now being prepared for them. God was the one apportioning it, ensuring each tribe received its rightful share. The inheritance flowed from His generous hand.

We should read the land promise in its proper place. It was a specific gift to Israel within God's covenant plan, not a promise of real estate for believers today. Yet the deeper truth of God as the giver of inheritance carries forward wonderfully. Our God delights to give good gifts to His people.

For those in Christ, God has prepared an inheritance far greater than any earthly land: an eternal inheritance that can never perish, spoil, or fade (1 Pet 1:4). It is kept in heaven for us, secured by Christ Himself. Lift your eyes beyond earthly portions to the inheritance God has prepared for all who trust in His Son.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you view God as a generous giver of good gifts?
2. How does the promise of an eternal inheritance shape your hope?
3. What does it mean that your inheritance in Christ can never fade?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Generous Father, thank You that You are the giver of every good gift. Lift my eyes beyond earthly things to the eternal inheritance You have prepared for me in Christ, kept secure in heaven. Amen.
